finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id calls authorized(), which returns a boolean instead of throwing, and ignores the result. Any authenticated user can delete any project (broken access control / IDOR). The sibling PUT route correctly uses authorize(), which throws.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /projects/<victim project id>. They do not need to be the owner or an admin.

trace.note: Project is loaded by id with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) returns true/false, and the return value is discarded, so nothing is enforced
authorized() only computes a boolean and never throws, unlike authorize() at api.js:4-10

finding.guards_checked: The router has no other middleware in this file, so no ownership check is applied elsewhere here. Any auth middleware that sets req.user is outside this file, and it would only establish identity, not ownership. The return value of authorized() is never checked. The PUT /projects/:id/name route is not affected, because authorize() throws there. A nonexistent id makes project undefined, so the handler throws a TypeError, which is only a minor robustness issue.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and never throws. Its result is discarded at api.js:18. No other middleware appears in this file. Any auth middleware that sets req.user is outside the file and could only establish identity.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() (api.js:12-14) as a bare statement, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated user, unlike authorize() at api.js:4-10 and its use at api.js:25.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18, so nothing is enforced. No other middleware or check exists in this directory.
verdict_facts.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() (api.js:12-14) and discards the result, so any authenticated user reaches req.store.projects.delete at api.js:19 for any project; the throwing authorize() is used only on the PUT route at api.js:25.
